parameters.name: uone
parameters.description: `uone = 60` U_1 is a round input scale chosen before fitting, comparable to the training input magnitude, solely for conditioning; it is not a fitted threshold.

parameters.name: utwo
parameters.description: `utwo = 20` U_2 is a round input scale chosen before fitting, comparable to the training input magnitude, solely for conditioning; it is not a fitted threshold.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Feedback magnitude, jointly fitted; see expression for whether it multiplies a state difference or a dimensionless logarithm.

parameters.name: g
parameters.description: Dimensionless first-input feedback modifier or sigmoid location, as specified by the expression.

parameters.name: ybase
parameters.description: Fitted reference state, not assumed to be an independently measured physical equilibrium.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Magnitude of the second-input forcing at normalized input unity.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Dimensionless fitted exponent of the nonnegative normalized second input.

estimation.criterion: Minimize the unweighted sum of squared simulated-minus-logged `y` residuals at every post-initial sample in each complete trajectory. This matches the evaluation objective and was selected by the internal suffix simulation comparison.
estimation.data: Final parameter estimation uses every derivative row of data/train.csv and data/val.csv as two separate trajectories. Where rollout residuals enter, it also uses all states after the first of each trajectory. Initial structural searches fitted data/train.csv only and compared free-running simulation on data/val.csv. A subsequent criterion comparison fitted the full training file plus zero-based validation rows 0 through 727 and evaluated rows 728 through 1453, with an independent measured initialization at row 728. The suffix was then included in the final refit to use all supplied identification information. No test data were accessed. No rows were discarded in the final fit.
estimation.method: The preliminary training derivative fit used bounded trust-region reflective nonlinear least squares, scipy.optimize.least_squares, from `k = 0.17999999999999999`, `g = 1.3`, `ybase = 0.98999999999999999`, `source = 0.012`, `n = 1.7`, `width = 0.20000000000000001`. This single start was chosen near the preliminary affine-rate magnitude and a broad normalized-input transition. No random seed applies. Bounds for the preliminary and final model were `k` in `[0.001, 0.55000000000000004]` 1/s; `g` in `[0.10000000000000001, 3]` -; `ybase` in `[0.69999999999999996, 1.3]` U_y; `source` in `[0, 0.5]` U_y/s; `n` in `[0.20000000000000001, 8]` -; `width` in `[0.01, 2]` -. They are numerical identification constraints allowing broad reference states and positive source/exponent/rate, not supplied physical information. The final solution does not reach these bounds. The final solver starts were `k = 0.11030766182657555`, `g = 1.0783186855452496`, `ybase = 0.9723301518380012`, `source = 0.013033110629379265`, `n = 1.5492978006134905`, `width = 0.17380787489798508`, taken from mode 3 derivative in clamped_results.json because the prior derivative fit was already in a reasonable local basin. Final and criterion-comparison fits use scipy.optimize.least_squares with trust-region reflective, `x_scale = "jac"`, maximum 800 function evaluations, and dimensionless tolerances `ftol = 1e-10`, `xtol = 1e-10`, `gtol = 1e-10`. Nonlinear least squares supports the free-running residual criterion, for which a linear coefficient solve is not available. No random numbers enter this final step. Criterion selection compared derivative-only least squares, rollout-only least squares, and joint least squares with derivative residuals multiplied by `10*sqrt(w)` s for dimensionless trial weights `w = 1` and `w = 10`. The 10 s residual scale is a chosen conditioning/tradeoff scale, not an identified time constant. The criterion with smallest suffix rollout RMSE was selected. Every rollout uses classical RK4 with 5 s steps, logged inputs held constant, and a single first-state initialization, never later measured-state resets. All fitted parameters are jointly reestimated at each fitting stage; intermediate estimates are not frozen.

discussion.family: Gain-scheduled first-order relaxation with a logistic input-dependent rate and power-law forcing. General nonlinear-model reference: O. Nelles, Nonlinear System Identification, Springer, 2001 (bibliographic reference recalled from memory, not externally checked).
discussion.interpretation: The state `y`, inputs `x1` and `x2`, and target `dy` are the logged columns. Their physical units are unknown. `U_y`, `U_1` and `U_2` below denote unspecified native units of `y`, `x1` and `x2`; `dy` has units `U_y/s`. In `-k*(y-ybase)/(1+exp(((x1/uone)-g)/width))+source*Max(x2/utwo,0)**n`, the first term pulls the state toward the reference with an always-positive rate, decreasing with the first input. The second term supplies positive power-law forcing. The logistic modulation is bounded and mathematically removes the sign change of the affine feedback model; no particular physical switching mechanism is claimed. The nonnegative input extension protects fractional powers.
discussion.origin: Affine-rate models fit well but permit negative rates outside their apparent crossing. A guessed logistic rate was explored as a stable-for-fixed-input alternative, distinct from sigmoid equilibria with constant rates. It has somewhat higher residual error but avoids state-feedback sign reversal. Its transition parameters and power forcing were identified from data; the choice of sigmoid was a stability assumption. In the internal criterion comparison, the best suffix rollout RMSE was 0.058685597 U_y on rows 728 through 1453 of data/val.csv, initialized only at row 728 (zero-based rows). This suffix was excluded from that fitting stage but had already been inspected in exploratory validation, so this is not a pristine independent estimate. After refitting on both complete files, the training and validation rollout RMSE values are 0.038834875 and 0.042076554 U_y; these final values are in-sample, not unseen-data scores. Final predicted-minus-logged derivative residual lag-one correlations are 0.661217 and 0.579239 (dimensionless) on training and validation, respectively.
discussion.limitations: There is no supplied physical description or intended use; no term is assigned a physical mechanism. This is a scalar autonomous-in-state, memoryless-in-input approximation, not evidence that omitted dynamics are absent. It cannot represent input histories, disturbances or time-dependent hidden states. Observed derivative residual correlation motivated nonlinear feedback and input-rate interactions, but remained after these extensions. Sampled derivatives need not be exact continuous-time derivatives, and integration-method effects are absorbed into fitted values. Extrapolation beyond the sampled state/input ranges is unverified; uncertainty intervals were not estimated. A positive instantaneous rate is not a guarantee that arbitrarily high source inputs keep the state inside the evaluation limits. The rate approaches zero at high first input, so long transients and very high equilibria are possible.
